SHINYMOD Arm Sleeves for Men Women UV Sun Protection Compression Warmer Cover I work 10-12 hours a day, and I'm outside in between white concrete structures all day. Too thin, too short, too cheap feeling, it just a basic failure of quality control in the "finished" product. But I kept buying them in the hopes that I'd find a decent brand because I NEED them. Even in December, the sun will be strong enough to burn in 30 minutes even if it's below freezing.

So I decided to try these SHINYMOD sleeves, and I'm so happy I did! They are amazing. Nice seams, soft, and stretchy enough that even when I have them pulled all the way up to my shoulder (and I have long arms), they are still not all the way stretched.

These are NOT light material, at least when compared to the dozens of other pairs I've purchased. But even though they are a little thicker, they do an incredible job of wicking sweat add c you have lots of room to adjust.

The thumbholes are super cool, abs like everything else about them, the perfect details come together to make the PERFECT product. Buy these. You'll be glad you did.

Yes these cost more than your average water bottle, but honestly, they've saved me a ton of money in the long run because I've not had to replace ever few months like all other water bottles I've used.

Nautilus R616 Recumbent Bike (Discontinued) This bike comes in a large box that makes it obvious what’s inside of it. If you have people that might steal your packages around, you might want to make arrangements to be there when this arrives. It’s on the heavy side, also, so the mail person might appreciate some help, too! ;)

You’ll have to assemble it, so make sure you set aside a good hour/hour and a half to put it together. It’s pretty simple and straightforward, though.

This bike has Bluetooth connectivity, but we never could get proper connection. Thankfully, the bike works perfectly fine without it. My husband has a Bluetooth device, but I don’t. That means we can both use it, with or without Bluetooth(should it ever connect properly).

One feature I like is that the seat slides back and forth with ease. While sitting on the seat, just pull down a little bar beside the seat, and slide it into the perfect position. Then, just push the bar back up to lock the seat in place. This makes the bike work for lots of various positions and leg lengths.

The main part of the bike comes fully assembled. (It’s the seat and top and all that needs assembly.) At one point, I was pedaling along and I started hearing a rattling noise. I became worried, thinking the bike was already messed up. Thankfully, it was only one of the circle pieces around the pedal that had popped off. I had to turn it a bit to lock it back into place. This part and most of the base is plastic, so I’m a bit concerned about the lasting quality of it.

The power cord is detachable. To me, that gives it a bit of a cheaper feel, but at the same time, it does make it easier with little ones around. When not in use, I can roll up the cord and tuck it out of sight, and no one is tripping around cords. But, once again, I’m a little concerned about the lasting quality of such a “light” power cord.

Overall, though, it’s a pretty nice bike. It’s comfortable to use, and for a piece of exercise equipment, it really doesn’t take up a ton of space.
text_fidelity_b: Nautilus R616 Recumbent Bike (Discontinued)

text_fidelity_a: Coghlans Waterproof Matches 10 Pack These are very good waterproof matches - as good as any other set I've ever used.  Bear in mind, however, they aren't magical.  It's still difficult to keep anything alight in a driving rain or heavy winds.  And, yes, they will not light if the striking surface is ruined, if struck under water, or in the vacuum of space.  For waterproof matches, they are very good.  As a fire starter, matches - in general - are adequate.  These should be kept in a nicer sealed matchbox with a protected striking surface (Coghlans makes a nice one that also includes a whistle and signal mirror), and you should have AT LEAST one other backup fire source that might mitigate the shortfalls of matches, if designated for a situation where fire starting is critical.  I never have less than three, when I go off-trail - usually waterproof matches, a [[ASIN:B0013L8D9K Swedish Firesteel]], usually a lighter or two, and sometimes a fire piston along with some good emergency tinder.  I wouldn't feel right with just one of any of these firestarters.
text_fidelity_b: Coghlans Waterproof Matches 10 Pack

text_fidelity_a:
Sportline 385 Digital Tally Counter (Chrome) Anyone working out on an indoor track will find a counter helpful. At 12 laps a mile, counting laps is difficult. Counting is easy; remembering how many laps I've done is hard.

The Sportline counter fixes what my math teacher could not, allowing me to turn my mental energies toward my workout, or toward a conversation with my running partner.

---Necessary on a Practical Level---
I tried a system of using my fingers on my right hand to measure laps 1-5, then using my left hand to measure how many laps in groups of five. That is, two fingers on my left and three fingers on my right would equal 13 laps. It sounds easier to employ than it actually is.

The Sportline counter has five worthwhile features:
* It counts one per click, up to 9,999. I won't run more than that, so, for me, it is plenty.
* The display is legible while running. The white digits are large, on a black background.
* The size of the device is small enough to carry.
* The finger loop fits nicely in my middle finger.
* The reset dial quickly zeroes out the counter.

The only two drawbacks are
* The reset dial would be more comfortably located on the left, not the right side of the counter, or otherwise better engineered for right-handed users.
* The weight is heavy. It is small, but can feel like baggage during a longer workout.

The Sportline counter is sturdy, does as advertised, and serves well as a tool for anyone walking or running a lot of laps.

Anthony Trendl
editor, HungarianBookstore.com
text_fidelity_b: Sportline 385 Digital Tally Counter (Chrome)

text_fidelity_a:
SHIMANO CS-6500 Ultegra Bicycle Cassette (9-Speed) I'm an intermediate level cyclist who recently moved to the Denver area. After nearly dying on a 2800 foot climb over 15 miles I noticed my riding buddy had about a gear and a half lower than me. I looked around and finally swapped my stock Ultegra 12/23 to this 12/27 on my 1998 Specialized Allez Sport with a triple crank (52-42-30).

After pricing the extra tools I needed to do a swap, it wasn't much more $ to just hand this cassette and a new chain to my local bike shop and have them do the work - still saved $50-$60 using my own parts. Since I have a triple, I also have a long derailleur, so besides the chain, there's nothing more needed for the swap except for adjusting the derailleur for the bigger sprocket. I think 27 is as big as I can go, BTW, given the range of teeth on my crank.

I haven't been back to that hill yet, but this cassette and new chain are doing fine so far. My second gear (running middle ring) is now like my first gear was. Given the 12T top end, I didn't give up any high gearing, but I do need to get used to the bigger jump between 5th and 6th gear (I think that's the spot).

My riding buddy has a double with an 11-speed cassette. I think we're pretty close on highest and lowest ratios now. Sorry, I don't recall what he's got. But its a fairly high end bike with 11x2.
text_fidelity_b: SHIMANO CS-6500 Ultegra Bicycle Cassette (9-Speed)

My wife and I are thrilled to have it! A few months ago my wife several broke her foot and has been off it. As the doctor lets her get back on it - and encourages slow exercise to help her rebuild leg muscles, I wanted to find something for her to do that would get her up, but not over do it. Bocce Ball can be played over a very large area - we controlled it by just going back and forth - but it got us outside, into the sun, and moving. She could take breaks and we had a blast! I grabbed the regulation set - figuring it was best overall for weight and size. I have never played before and she hadn’t played since she was a teen. We had to use the instructions, but it was pretty easy to learn. And our local park was the perfect place.

1. It comes in a great bag - the full set fits well into the bag, which is well designed and built. It’s a strong material, looks great - with the logo - and the zipper is strong. This is a pretty heavy set of balls and this bag holds up well. It looks great out there too.
2. There are three nets in the bag, each holding 3 balls - or two balls and the small ball and measuring string.
3. There is a set of instructions - my wife read it and talked me through it. It’s been easy to learn and play.
4. The balls for this set weigh a great amount - it wasn’t long before we had a feel for them and able to play well - a difference between long play or short.
5. The balls can take it. In this state the ground is a bit hard and the grass isn’t the best, and we were throwing them a good distance. After 3 games over 2 days they still look perfect. I’m not saying we beat them up, but we put them through playing - these are really nice. They look nice, hold nice, have a great balance. I really have no game of reference, but this is a great set.

I literally played for the first time this weekend and I loved it! This was a great game for my wife and I - not just as she recovers from her foot injury, but in general. We have every intention of getting many years out of this set - playing often. We took it easy because of her recovery, but we know we’ll be able to cover a lot of ground in the future (grass, sand, whatever). It is a fun game with a need for some talent - but yet something most nay member of the family can play. Our regulation set is fairly heavy - we are guessing not as heavy as tournament - so something to consider if playing with kids. But we have had a lot of fun, shared a lot of laughs, and enjoyed spending the time playing. We are thrilled with this JAPER BEES Bocce Ball Set and look forward to many more years playing.

Me, I have balance issues so instead of standing, I wade out a few feet into the water, get myself seated on the paddleboard and with my legs dangling in the water, I paddle is that seated position.  I had looked at different ways to enjoy the lake - an inner tube you just float and while it's nice to kind of lay back and float, you can't really be proactive in getting yourself here or there in an inner tube.  I really looked at kayaks seriously (and the prices are way out of my price range), but getting in a kayak is a bit more tricky than this paddleboard.  So this is paddleboard, while it is larger and more suited to my nephew, is still a wonderful board that I would have kept had I not found one that fit my frame better.  For taller folks, this is a great board that comes with everything you need to have fun on the water!

I thought this balance bike would be great for them, especially as the older child is still so nervous about balancing her bike on her own. The younger niece was so excited, but even at the lowest setting, it seemed to be difficult for her to "walk" to bike with both feet while sitting on the seat. She's almost walking on tip-toe. She's big for her age. She also didn't seem to like the hard seat and found it uncomfortable. It'll probably fit her better at age 3. The older niece wanted a try, so we put the seat at the max height line. She's about average height for her age, but she was too large to use it to learn to balance on 2 wheels. It was awkward for her to walk it and will be difficult to coast it even if she lifts her legs outward (as she can't use the built in foot rest). So we're a little disappointed. (UPDATE: Actually, the older girl can coast on it and has gotten quite good at balancing, but it's still awkward for her and she complains that the seat is uncomfortable. The pictures show the 5 year-old.)

The assembly instructions were a couple of crowded diagrams with the brief text instructions on a different page. The text added nothing to the diagrams. I was getting ready to put the bike together before the nieces arrived to visit when my dad (grandpa) saw what I was doing and took over. He promptly proved that you can't just guess about how it should go together and then, yes, you really do need to align the pieces the way shown in the diagram. However, once he started following the diagram, we did hit snag with the handlebar section. The front wheel comes up through the shaft and the handlebars go down in the shaft, then you tighten a band over both to hold things in place. It wasn't until the plastic spacer on the wheel section was removed that enough of the bottom pipe was exposed for this band to effectively tighten over and hold everything in place and aligned. It looks sturdy now that it's together.

text_fidelity_a:
TosGad Yellow Sunglasses for Men, Polarized Reduce Glare and Enhance Vision in Rainy, Foggy UPDATE: We've had rain today so wore these out - have to say, they were great. Please read on for my earlier thoughts regarding them overall and night, but I am adding this - I like them. We are in a state that rainy weather can cause glares and that gray palate that makes elements blend together. We also have a rainy season over 4 months, so it is something that causes me to sometimes wear sunglasses in order to see better. But that makes it even darker. I put these on and it brightened everything. Had my wife try and she too felt there was a brightness. She didn't like them in that she didn't loose the glare per se, however, I did. But for rain, I will most certainly use them - night time, I'm still 50/50.

I had lasik eye surgery a number of years ago and ever since when I drive at nights, lights have “star bursts” and while I can see easily, it’s a bit of a stressor on my eyes - the bright lights can make me squint. So I saw these - and many like them over the months - and I thought I’d give them a try. No idea why, but why not.

1. They fit well and look somewhat cool - though my wife has now refereed to me as George Michael several times. I like them.

2. I don’t know that they work. Or what they are supposed to work for. But, they do something.
I feel it like this: there are those bright white-blue LED lights in many homes now. You can see them stand out brightly - apart from the softer, warmer, yellow or orange lights we grew up with. When I drive/walk/am out at night I can see fine with the white-blue cold lights, but I’ll find myself squinting against them at times, even feeling stress on my eyes from the harshness of them. But with these glasses, they warm and soften these bright white-blue, cold lights and make them more like the softer, warmed, yellow-orange ones. This cuts my squinting and feeling of stress. So Yes, they DO something and DO work, but I’m not even sure if that’s what’s supposed to be happening. It’s what I experience.

3. I still see star bursts on lights, these have not changed that at all. I have not worn in rain yet, but if there is any similarity, they only change the coloring, they do not make anything. sharper, easier to see, or enhanced. But they DO something that makes it a little more comfortable.

I can’t give them a 5 because while they do something I honestly thought they’d do more. I fell like that is the implication. But, I also did feel a bit of stress relief and comfort in these over the sharpness of the LED bright white-blue increasingly on the roads and signage. So I have to give them 4 because I did feel something positive.
text_fidelity_b: TosGad Yellow Sunglasses for Men, Polarized Reduce Glare and Enhance Vision in Rainy, Foggy

SIQIJUN Valgens D Shape Spring-Loaded Gate Aluminum Carabiner for Home, Rv, Camping, Fishing, Hiking, Traveling and Keychain Small Size(Assorted Colors) These carabineers are functional and have a use, so long as you realize how teeny tiny they are. Each one is only slightly larger than a quarter. They cannot hold a full set of keys but would be ideal for holding one or two standard metal keys. (My minimalist hubby loves things this small and simple.) I feel they would be great for suspending an extra key and hanging it from the branch of a tree so you always have a hidden spare.

I'm not joking when I say they are the midget love child of a carabiner and a paperclip. We have some little carabineers floating around the house but these are smaller than any I have ever seen. If your daughter needs a carabiner for her American Girl Doll, you've come to the right place!

All joking aside, these are great for securing small items to your purse or backpack such as hand sanitizer, lip balm holders and other small incidentals. The carabineers have a sporty look to them and are sure to draw a few "Aww! A tiny baby carabineer!" comments from random strangers. They don't open wide enough to hold the back strap of a hat (max opening is 0.4 inches - less than 1/2 inch). I suspect they will last longer if they aren't opened repeatedly but only used to suspend lightweight items. They are ideal if you need to loan out a single key and provide a way for the borrower to not lose the key. They would also be a great way to quickly attach luggage tags to bags and should hold up to minor wear and tear.

All five of mine were delivered working with paint finishes that were in very good shape. The pink (my favorite) is already starting to show some signs of the paint rubbing away and revealing the shiny silver aluminum underneath from use.I was kind of bummed that I received a cobalt blue instead of an aqua blue bineer.

I was fortunate to be able to receive this set of 5 for free to write a review. If you are aware of the tiny size and lightweight duty carabineer you are buying, the product is accurately represented.

We tried it out at our scout meeting to see if the Campfire & 2 pot set held up to the hype. We had no trouble lighting the fire with a piece of pine lighter with some small twigs off the ground.

Small amount of smoke when the fire was first ignited, less than a few minutes the fire was almost smokeless as the fire was consuming the wood efficiently.

I did have one defect in the product as a spot weld on the cooking ring wasn’t made and was loose. After contacting the company they quickly sent out a replacement cooking ring to replace the loose ring. Primal Treestands Wraith 270 Deluxe Blind - 270 Degree One-Way, See-Through Pop-Up Tent 3 Person, Premium Hunting Gear Sporting Good First, this is most important to understand. FOLLOW THE INSTRUCTIONS or you will have hell to pay setting up unless you are very lucky. If you already have a blind you know how vicious they can be to get up. Or mebbe it's just me. Ha. The instructions say clearly to pop the top first. You MUST identify the top. My top pull loop now has a brightly colored piece of cloth on it. Pop the top first and then pop pop pop, it's up in under 45 seconds. Get that right or suffer.
Now for the great part. The view from inside is absolutely phenomenal. From a lawn chair I had a panoramic view unequaled. AND at the RIGHT height. And from the outside you can't see a doggone thing. Lots of room for one, enough for two. From the inside a clear view all around and even a little flap in the back. On those three sides it's made so you can stick a barrel or an arrow out easily. No shooting through the webbing.
I'll tell you one thing it didn't have. No pinholes in the roof like my other one. It's solid. I don't know how much protection it will be in a driving rain, but straight down, it's not going to leak.
If you're new to popup blinds you can pretty much discard the tie down stakes. You'll end up getting something more substantial to peg it but that goes for all popups that I'm aware of. A friend put me onto the perfect cheap solution. Nail spikes. (Really big nails.) You can get them at most any hardware store.I selected the 10 inchers.
Especially if you have hunted pop up blinds before the Primal Treestands Wraith 270 Deluxe Blind is going to blow you away. A VERY well thought out system. I very much recommend this one.
And PS...take down was a complete snap. Top down, pop pop pop. It did kinda take two to get it back in the bag...me to give it the old bear hug while the other slipped the bag up. It's a good piece of equipment!
text_fidelity_b: Primal Treestands Wraith 270 Deluxe Blind - 270 Degree One-Way, See-Through Pop-Up Tent 3 Person, Premium Hunting Gear Sporting Good

They also had itchy straps that she said bothered her when she sweat so I knew it was time to test some new brands. They fit her perfectly and provide great protection/coverage as a midfielder and also goalkeeper. I've washed the mesh sleeves a handful of times now and hang dry them; there has been no snags or tears yet and the shin guards have held up really well. text_fidelity_a:
Bike Handlebar Mirror 2 Pack - Rotatable And Adjustable Wide Angle Rear View Shockproof Convex Mirror Universal For Bike Bicycle I like these mirrors, I typically ride against traffic, as it's easier to keep a lookout for drivers. The thing is, when someone is coming, I have to look over and see what the other lane is doing. That isn't always comfy, and I sometimes don't feel safe having to look over my shoulder. That's why I don't ride with traffic, because it's too often I have to look over myself to see what's behind me.

These mirrors help for both types of riding, but the problem is that even with them, it's hard to really see them until they're really close on you. It's better to have them than not, but it requires focusing on the mirrors to see a car from a fair bit away. I like the look of them, and the mounting isn't too bad, it has rubber pieces you can put into it to clamp down with, and once you do that, they're pretty stable. You do have really good visibility, and even if I can't see the cars from far away, it's a really pretty sight being able to see the world passing by you behind you. I like these, but I took a star off just because I wished I could see the cars better. Maybe if they were magnified they'd work better. Do get them, but if needing quick visibility on the cars behind you is very important, skip these, look for magnified mirrors more similar to car mirrors.
text_fidelity_b: Bike Handlebar Mirror 2 Pack - Rotatable And Adjustable Wide Angle Rear View Shockproof Convex Mirror Universal For Bike Bicycle

But when I relied it in I could see the stretched coils that formed when I tied my knots. I use two different knots, and they've literally never failed me. Not even with braided line.

So I guess the choice is yours. The line won't snap off any more easily than with any other line. But once I've lost faith in a line's ability to hold a tried and true set of knots, it will be hard for me to be confident enough to use it ever again.

EDIT: I've found out that this stuff makes pretty decent VB 6X or 8X tippets for fly-fishing. By using either double uni or double surgeon's knots, the difficulty with knot integrity is mitigated. The line is plenty strong, so this is actually a great value for tippet material.
